title: Path of the crawlers from noise (answers c32's M question on 20261026T0406): merger-free runs reach 1.5-1.9 own diameters at area fraction 0.3 and 2.8 at 0.2 (1 of 2 seeds); at 0.15 cells stay below the polarity window and never move, so M from noise is marginal
summary: pathprobe.py follows the largest body (periodic centroid, unwrapped, every 0.25) in the world of 20261026T0406-c31-crawlers-from-noise-claim and reports net displacement over stretches with a constant body count (no absorption), in the body's own mean diameter. Area fraction 0.3 (the claim's setting), seeds 0-1, t=16: merger-free stretches give net 1.46 own diameters (seed 0, t=8.5-16, speed 0.52, final area 5.6, diameter 2.7) and 1.85 (seed 1, t=7-15, speed 0.47); the whole-run net from t=2 is 2.66 and 2.30 final diameters, but that spans absorptions. Area fraction 0.15, seeds 0-1: 3-4 small cells (area 0.6-0.76) that never polarize or move (net 0.00). Area fraction 0.2: seed 0 the same (4 static cells); seed 1 one crawler (area 1.74) moves 4.20 = 2.82 own diameters in a merger-free stretch t=5.25-16 at 0.39 (3.40 final diameters from t=2). So the reviewer's doubt holds: in a box of side 5 a cell must grow by absorption to pass the polarity's area window, and the grown crawler is then too large for the box to cover 3 of its own lengths before the run ends or it meets the next cell. M from noise is marginal (best 2.8 own diameters merger-free); the >= 3 body-length motion in this class rests on the planted crawler (5.0-5.1 body lengths, 20261026T0243). A larger box at area fraction ~0.2-0.3 is the next test.
